title: Ledger record: hand_turn_definition
description: The human's DEFINITION of what counts as a hand-turn, and at which stage (issue #319, decision c25). An observing agent proposes `hand_turn` records against it and names it in `definition_ref`; the human iterates the definition from what the agent got wrong. Like every other record it is written proposed and confirmed through a review transaction -- the person who wrote it is the person who confirms it, through the same surface, so the ledger shows the definition was ratified rather than merely typed. A correction is a new record with `supersedes` pointing at the old one, never an edit.

stages.description: The loop stages a hand-turn may be filed under, in loop order (e.g. dispatch, land, review, cleanup).

stage.description: Which of `stages` a match is filed under.

description.description: The rule in the human's words (e.g. `a commit on the PR branch with no run attempt in the window`).

rules.description: What the observer recognises. Any matcher parameters (patterns, windows) are additional properties of a rule; the schema pins only what makes a rule citable.

notes.description: Why the definition is what it is, for the next person iterating it.
